name: Technical Sans and Mono
description: IBM Plex Mono SemiBold headings and numerals and Medium labels, quotes, and code, over a neutral system sans body on a technical scale.

provenance.attribution: IBM Plex Mono, by IBM, self-hosted from its pinned npm package for the keyurgolani.name portfolio platform.
provenance.copyright: Copyright © 2017 IBM Corp. with Reserved Font Name "Plex"
provenance.maintainer: The upstream project, at the version fonts.provenance.json pins
provenance.derivation: The prototype's technical-sans-mono stacks on LANG-5b's technical scale, its monospace roles in IBM Plex Mono ahead of their system stacks (Mono (b)): Medium and SemiBold, copied unmodified from IBM's split WOFF2 in @ibm/plex-mono 2.5.0, never subset or renamed inside.

fallbacks: IBM Plex Mono is followed by metric-matched fallback faces over local system fonts (size-adjust and ascent, descent, and line-gap overrides), then the system monospace stack it had and a generic family.
There's a fallback face at each weight the mono roles set, 500 and 600.
Glyphs outside Plex's unicode-range render in the declared system stack, so text never goes missing.
The sans roles, body, body-compact, and caption, are system stacks that end in a generic family, so a platform without the named fonts renders its own.
caveats: IBM Plex Mono ships at 500, for labels, quotes, and code, and 600, for headings and numerals, and covers Latin-1 alone.
The sans roles are system fonts: they fall back to what each platform installs.

A Latin page loads 35,740 B of font. Letters outside Latin-1, such as ő or ł, set in the system monospace stack: SF Mono in Safari on macOS, Menlo in other Mac browsers, Consolas on Windows, and Liberation Mono or the platform's own monospace on Linux.
